science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 4,100 K and log g 4.36 (u1 0.724, u2 0.065): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used. The disc is unresolved: no map or absolute brightness is implied. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Sep 2012
science.description: Radial component of the star's large-scale magnetic field, fitted with ZDIpy to 16 ESPaDOnS spectra of 25 September 2012 to 1 October 2012 (reduced chi-square 1.10, against 23.5 with no field); mean field 133 G. A reduction made in this project, not a published map. Black line: 39 degrees south, below which the star never faces us.
science.title: ESPaDOnS · magnetic map made here · Sep 2012

science.label: Sector 4
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 4.71 days, fitted with starry to the TESS mission's own 2-minute light curve of sector 4 (its PDC-MAP flux) (the light varies by 11%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 0.91%, the light's own noise being 0.17%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. In this sector the method of Holcomb et al. (2022, ApJ 936, 138) finds a period of 4.92 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.39, a width of 0.47 and a fit of 1.00, and in all 5 of the star's sectors together a period of 4.71 d from the autocorrelation, whose peaks have a height of 0.42, a width of 0.51 and a fit of 1.00; its criteria accept that as the star's rotation. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 39°. Gaia DR3 lists no other star within 63 arcseconds of it. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · brightness map made here · Sector 4

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffc9a7, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in TESS sector 71 (October and November 2023): the map's scale, 50% to 150% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 58.4% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: TESS · the star in its color over its brightness map · October and November 2023
